summary: Grade red: 2 red, 3 yellow, 1 green findings in 9 files.

findings.title: Custom CUDA source
findings.action: Port this CUDA source by hand. Evaluate HIPIFY (AMD's CUDA-to-HIP translator) and SCALE (a toolchain that compiles CUDA for AMD GPUs) as starting points, then rebuild and test on the AMD machine. portcheck does not translate kernels.

findings.title: TensorRT
findings.action: TensorRT runs only on NVIDIA GPUs. A person must replace this code path with one that works on ROCm, for example plain PyTorch, ONNX Runtime with the MIGraphX or ROCm provider, or MIGraphX directly, and re-validate the outputs.

findings.title: NVIDIA base image
findings.action: Swap the base image to a ROCm PyTorch image (target.rocm_image in portcheck.yaml).

findings.title: NVML or nvidia-smi call
findings.action: NVML and nvidia-smi exist only on NVIDIA machines. Guard the import so the code still loads elsewhere, and make each call site handle a missing NVML (on AMD, rocm-smi or amd-smi report the same kind of data).

findings.title: NVIDIA pip pins
findings.action: Remove the NVIDIA-only pip packages and point any CUDA wheel index at the PyTorch ROCm index (target.torch_index_url in portcheck.yaml).

findings.title: Plain torch.cuda usage
findings.action: No change needed. ROCm builds of PyTorch use the same torch.cuda API.
